ACT TWO: The Prince and the Ghost duel for the King's fate.
[Margin: 'They are clearly in love. Write it in or I will. - M.Q.']
ACT THREE: The Dragon.
[Margin: 'Needs a dragon. A better one. - M.Q.']
ACT FOUR: The Great Speech.

    Though the ledger strike my name, though the ink run dry,
    Though every clerk in every hall forget that I was I,
    I stand here still, I breathe here still, and this I swear:
    A name held true by one who loves is never truly bare.

    I AM COUNTED.

[Margin, in very small, shaky red letters: 'This bit is good. - M.']
strings.item.mask_uncounted.name: Mask of the Uncounted King
strings.item.mask_uncounted.description: The gilded half-mask you wore on opening night. Odette insisted you keep it. When you wear it, people turn to look at you, and for once you don't mind. +3 Presence, +5% spell power, +3% critical chance.
strings.item.thrown_tomato.name: Thrown Tomato
strings.item.thrown_tomato.description: Caught mid-air during the curtain call. A critic's gift. Still perfectly good to eat, and oddly motivating: +0.2 critical multiplier for 2 minutes.
strings.item.paper_crown.name: Paper Crown
strings.item.paper_crown.description: Folded from the dust jacket of a romance novel. Chapter Nine is printed on the inside. Wear it facing forward.
strings.item.dragon_costume.name: Dragon Costume
strings.item.dragon_costume.description: Leather scales, oilcloth wings, real glass eyes. Ordered nine years ago by a monster hunter 'for a contract'. It watches you.
strings.item.fireworks.name: Sabrino's Fireworks
strings.item.fireworks.description: Gold, green, purple, and one labelled THE GOOSE. Do not ask about The Goose.
strings.item.thunder_sheet.name: Thunder Sheet (Confiscated)
strings.item.thunder_sheet.description: A great sheet of tin. Shake firmly for weather. Comes with a receipt.
strings.comp.kaelen.zone.bellwether: Bellwether. Population: one hundred and six, last I counted. Plus you. I'm counting you now.
strings.comp.kaelen.zone.old_road: Home. Mind the third stone from the arch, it wobbles. I've written it down.
strings.comp.kaelen.zone.annex: So this is where they kept the names. It smells like a library that's been holding its breath.
strings.comp.kaelen.zone.vault_three: Forty small beds. I'm going to count them anyway. Someone should.
strings.comp.kaelen.zone.seal_chamber: This is the room the whole Marches has been leaning on. Walk softly.
strings.comp.kaelen.zone.hollowmere: Hollowmere. The Ashbound have three pages on this house. Two of them are about the gardener.
strings.comp.kaelen.zone.hollowmere_manor: Twelve places laid at the table. I'll note that. Twelve's a hopeful number.
strings.comp.kaelen.idle.1: Every stone on this road was somebody's doorstep once. I keep a list.
strings.comp.kaelen.idle.2: The Ashbound have a rule: if you can't remember something, write it down twice.
strings.comp.kaelen.idle.3: I counted the steps from the boundary stone to the Annex once. Four thousand and twelve. Then I lost count, because a rat bit me.
strings.comp.kaelen.idle.4: You walk like someone who's used to being alone. It's all right. You'll get out of the habit.
strings.comp.kaelen.idle.5: Ash is what's left when something burns. It still remembers the shape of the wood. That's us.
strings.comp.kaelen.idle.6: I've started writing your name in my journal. Every day. Just in case.
strings.comp.kaelen.idle.seal: The road doesn't hum any more. I miss it a little. Don't tell anyone.
strings.comp.kaelen.idle.ilse: Ilse Brannock. I've written it in four places now. Can't be too careful.
strings.comp.kaelen.idle.dinner: That dinner. I read the names out loud and the whole table said them back. I'll never forget that. Literally: I wrote it down.
strings.comp.kaelen.combat.3: Here they come. Note the time.
strings.comp.kaelen.combat.4: I've fought worse. I wrote it down.
strings.comp.kaelen.kill.1: One less. I'm keeping a tally.
strings.comp.kaelen.heal.1: Here. Ashbound trail bread. Tastes like a promise.
strings.comp.kaelen.heal.2: Sit. Eat. The road will still be there in a minute.
strings.comp.kaelen.level.1: Stronger. I'm putting that in the journal. In capitals.
strings.comp.kaelen.level.2: Look at you. The road's taught you something.
strings.comp.kaelen.catchup.1: Took the long way. Counted some wells. I'm back.
strings.comp.kaelen.catchup.2: Sorry. There was an interesting stone.
strings.comp.kaelen.catchup.3: Caught up. Baggy wasn't the only one stuck on that door.
strings.comp.kaelen.banter.intro.0: So, Kaelen. What's your story? Everybody has a story. I'm a detective. I can tell.
strings.comp.kaelen.banter.intro.1: I walk. I count things. I write them down.
strings.comp.kaelen.banter.intro.3: That's a lot, Baggy. Most people forget to do any of it.
strings.comp.kaelen.banter.counting.0: Baggy. How many suspects are on your case board right now?
strings.comp.kaelen.banter.counting.1: Four! The hedge, the Bureau, a goat, and me. I've ruled me out. Mostly.
strings.comp.kaelen.banter.counting.2: That's four more than I've got. I just count wells.
strings.comp.kaelen.banter.counting.3: What do the wells tell you?
strings.comp.kaelen.banter.counting.4: That somebody was thirsty once. That's enough, usually.
strings.comp.kaelen.banter.hedge.0: Kaelen. Be honest. Do you think the hedge did it?
strings.comp.kaelen.banter.hedge.1: I've walked past that hedge four hundred times. It has never once done anything.
strings.comp.kaelen.banter.hedge.2: EXACTLY. That's what a guilty hedge would do.
strings.comp.kaelen.banter.hedge.3: ...I'm adding the hedge to my journal. Under 'probably fine'.
strings.comp.kaelen.banter.ilse.0: Baggy. The girl with flour on her nose. Ilse.
strings.comp.kaelen.banter.ilse.1: Blue shutters. Mill Lane. I remember.
strings.comp.kaelen.banter.ilse.2: I wrote her name in my journal. And yours, next to it. 'Remembered her when nobody else did.'
strings.comp.kaelen.banter.ilse.3: ...Oh. Oh, I'm not crying. It's the rain.
strings.comp.kaelen.banter.hollowmere.0: So. The vampire and the werewolf at Hollowmere.
strings.comp.kaelen.banter.hollowmere.3: I KNOW. I've got two pages of notes. They've been staring at each other's windows for ninety years.
strings.comp.kaelen.banter.hollowmere.5: Somebody probably will. Somebody with terrible timing and a lot of heart.
strings.comp.kaelen.banter.theatre.0: Baggy, Odette says you've got a line in the play.
strings.comp.kaelen.banter.theatre.1: 'Who goes there.' It's a very demanding role.
strings.comp.kaelen.banter.dinner.0: Kaelen. At the dinner. When you read the names.
strings.comp.kaelen.banter.dinner.2: Everyone said them back. Even Oakhaven. Even Hollis.
strings.comp.kaelen.banter.dinner.3: I know. I was there. I was the one crying into the gnocchi.
strings.comp.kaelen.banter.dinner.4: I thought that was the pepper.
strings.comp.kaelen.banter.seal.0: The road's gone quiet. First time in seventeen years.
strings.comp.kaelen.banter.seal.2: Like taking off a heavy pack you forgot you were wearing.
strings.comp.kaelen.banter.seal.3: I've still got my umbrella. Out of habit. In case.
strings.comp.kaelen.banter.seal.4: Keep it. You never know. And it suits you.
strings.dlg.scout.choice_join: "Kaelen, travel with me for a while? I could use someone who remembers things."
strings.dlg.scout.choice_wait: "Could you wait here for a bit, Kaelen?"
strings.dlg.scout.join:
Kaelen closes the journal, slowly, and looks at you for a long moment.

"The Ashbound walk alone, mostly. It's quieter. Less to write down." A pause. "It's also lonelier, and I've been out here a long time."

The journal goes back on the belt. "All right. I'll walk with you. I'll count things. I'll keep the names. And if you get hurt, I've got trail bread. It tastes like a promise."

"Fair warning: if Baggy's coming too, I'm going to be asked about the hedge."
strings.dlg.scout.wait: "I'll be here. Counting." Kaelen opens the journal again. "Come and find me when the road gets long."
strings.dlg.baggy.party_full.choice: "Want to come along?" [Your party is full]
strings.dlg.baggy.party_full:
Baggy looks at your companion, then at you, then nods with tremendous professionalism. "Two's company. Three's a crowd. Four's a stakeout, but we haven't got the snacks for it."

"Ask someone to wait somewhere, and I'll be right there. I'm never busy. I'll be by the hedge."
strings.dlg.scout.party_full.choice: "Want to come along?" [Your party is full]
strings.dlg.scout.party_full:
Kaelen glances at whoever is already walking with you and makes a small note. "You've got company. Good. The road's better that way."

"When there's room, come and find me. I'll be here. Counting."
strings.dlg.dnd.topic.pitch: "Oakhaven, what do you do on Thursdays?"
strings.dlg.dnd.topic.s1: "Is it Thursday? Is it game night?"
strings.dlg.dnd.topic.s2: "Game night. The dungeon awaits, Game Master."
strings.dlg.dnd.pitch:
Oakhaven goes very still. He glances left, right, then lowers his voice as if confessing to a crime.

"On Thursdays, after the office closes, a few of us gather at the back table of the Lantern Inn and play... a game." He produces a battered rulebook roughly the thickness of a paving stone. "DUNGEONS & DEBTORS. A game of heroic adventure, perilous dungeons and meticulous record-keeping."

"I am the Game Master." He says it with a dignity you have never seen in him before. "We are short a player. Hollis cheats, Rolf cries, and Baggy keeps trying to arrest the furniture. Would you... care to roll up a character?"
strings.dlg.dnd.pitch.c0: "I would love to roll up a character."
strings.dlg.dnd.s0_rules:
Thursday. The back table of the Lantern Inn. Marta has put out bread, cheese and a pot of tea the size of a bucket. Around the table: Baggy, Rolf, Hollis, Lord Ashgrave ("I am only here for the atmosphere"), and Marta herself, pencil behind her ear.

Oakhaven sits behind a folding screen painted with dragons and tax tables. He hands you a sheet of paper.

OAKHAVEN (GM): "Form 1-CS. Character Sheet. Please print clearly. First, we roll your attributes. Four dice, drop the lowest. No, Hollis, you may not 'help'."

HOLLIS: "Hmm."
strings.dlg.dnd.s0_rules.c0: [Roll for Strength] Shake the dice in both hands and blow on them.
strings.dlg.dnd.s0_rules.c1: [Let Hollis roll for you] He's very insistent.
strings.dlg.dnd.s0_stats:
Sixteen! A respectable number. The table makes approving noises. Rolf claps. Baggy writes "16" in a notebook for reasons nobody understands.

OAKHAVEN (GM): "Excellent. Now. Your class."
strings.dlg.dnd.s0_stats_bad:
Four. You rolled a four. Two ones and a two and a... you check... another one.

There is a respectful silence around the table, the kind usually reserved for funerals.

MARTA (patting your hand): "You'll be a lovely character, dear. Characters with low numbers have the best stories."

OAKHAVEN (GM): "...Your class."
strings.dlg.dnd.s0_hollis:
Hollis takes your dice, turns his back to the table, and rolls. "Eighteen," he announces. "Eighteen. Eighteen. Eighteen. Eighteen. And an eighteen."

OAKHAVEN (GM): "Hollis, show me the dice."

HOLLIS: "They rolled under the table."

OAKHAVEN (GM): "All six of them?"

HOLLIS: "Hmm."

You are given a ten in everything. Hollis looks satisfied anyway.
strings.dlg.dnd.s0_class:
OAKHAVEN (GM): "Choose your class. Each is described in Chapter Four, pages eighty through four hundred."

BAGGY (whispering): "I'm a Paladin of Justice. I can arrest people with my mind."

ROLF (whispering): "I'm playing a human accountant called Gerald. It's the most exotic thing I can imagine."
strings.dlg.dnd.s0_class.c0: [Barbarian] Big. Angry. Shirtless. Rolf looks at you with new respect.
strings.dlg.dnd.s0_class.c1: [Bard] You will solve every problem by singing at it. Including the dragon.
strings.dlg.dnd.s0_class.c2: [Rogue] Sneaky, stabby, and you will absolutely steal from the party.
strings.dlg.dnd.s0_class.c3: [Wizard] Robes. Fireballs. A beard you have to describe in detail.
strings.dlg.dnd.s0_class.c4: [Paladin] Holy, righteous, and contractually obliged to lecture everyone.
strings.dlg.dnd.s0_backstory:
OAKHAVEN (GM): "And finally: your backstory. Briefly, please. Ashgrave's was forty-one pages."

LORD ASHGRAVE: "It was a tragedy in five movements."

OAKHAVEN (GM): "It was a tragedy in the sense that I had to read it."
strings.dlg.dnd.s0_backstory.c0: [Tragic] "Orphaned. Twice. My village burned. Also my second village. I have a brooding scar and a sworn enemy."
strings.dlg.dnd.s0_backstory.c1: [Simple] "Farmer. Nothing happened. I'm just here for the adventure."
strings.dlg.dnd.s0_backstory.c2: [Relatable] "Amnesiac. Legally dead. Owes burial tax. Nobody remembers them."
strings.dlg.dnd.s0_party:
One by one, the others introduce their characters, in character, with voices.

BAGGY: "Sir Detective Inspector Baggington, Paladin of Justice. I have a magnifying glass of plus-one perception."

ROLF: "Gerald. Human. Accountant. I enjoy spreadsheets and wearing shirts." He looks so happy about the shirts.

HOLLIS: "Grizzlebeard. Monster hunter. White hair. Two swords. Says 'hmm'."

OAKHAVEN (GM): "That's just you, Hollis."

HOLLIS: "Hmm."

LORD ASHGRAVE: "Lord Definitely-Not-A-Vampire. A paladin who avoids sunlight for entirely unrelated reasons."

MARTA: "Sister Crumb. A cleric. I heal with bread." She passes round actual bread. Everyone's hit points go up.
strings.dlg.dnd.s0_end:
OAKHAVEN (GM): "We start next Thursday. Character creation took four hours. It always takes four hours."

He gathers the sheets into a folder labelled CAMPAIGN: THE AMULET OF UNPAID TAXES, and almost, almost smiles.

"Same time next week. Bring dice. Bring snacks. Hollis, bring HONEST dice."
strings.dlg.dnd.s1_start:
Thursday again. The back table. The dragon screen goes up, Marta's tea goes round, and Oakhaven clears his throat.

OAKHAVEN (GM): "Session One. You all meet in a tavern."

A pause. Everyone looks around the Lantern Inn. At the bar. At Marta, pouring.

ROLF: "...We ARE in a tavern."

OAKHAVEN (GM): "Then this will be very immersive. A hooded stranger approaches your table." He pulls up the hood of his coat, without moving from behind the screen. "'Greetings, adventurers. I have a quest.'"
strings.dlg.dnd.s1_start.c0: [In character] "Speak, stranger. What do you need?"
strings.dlg.dnd.s1_start.c1: [Suspicious] "I roll Insight on the hooded stranger."
strings.dlg.dnd.s1_start.c2: [Out of character] "Oakhaven, that's just you in a hood."
strings.dlg.dnd.s1_insight:
OAKHAVEN (GM): "You sense that the hooded stranger is... the Game Master. In a hood."

HOLLIS: "I roll Insight too."

OAKHAVEN (GM): "He's still me, Hollis."

HOLLIS: "Hmm. Suspicious."
strings.dlg.dnd.s1_hood:
OAKHAVEN (GM): "It is NOT me. It is Mysterious Hooded Stranger Number Four. He has a completely different voice." He clears his throat and does a completely identical voice. "'Greetings, adventurers.'"

The table dissolves. Marta snorts tea out of her nose. Oakhaven waits it out with tremendous patience.
strings.dlg.dnd.s1_quest:
OAKHAVEN (GM, as the Stranger): "Deep beneath the hills lies the Dungeon of Mild Peril. Within it rests the Amulet of Unpaid Taxes, stolen from the Royal Treasury four hundred years ago by Debtrax the Insolvent, an ancient red dragon."

"Bring it back, and you shall be rewarded with five hundred gold pieces."

BAGGY (instantly): "I'd like to see some identification."

ROLF: "Gerald would like to know if the five hundred gold is taxable."

OAKHAVEN (GM, visibly delighted): "It IS, Gerald. Thank you for asking."

Just then, the door of the fictional tavern bursts open. A gang of fictional bandits stomps in, looking for trouble.
strings.dlg.dnd.s1_brawl: OAKHAVEN (GM): "Roll for initiative! Three bandits, one of them called Steve. What do you do?"
strings.dlg.dnd.s1_brawl.c0: [Barbarian] Pick up a table. Throw the table. Throw Steve.
strings.dlg.dnd.s1_brawl.c1: [Bard] Sing a song so moving the bandits lay down their weapons and weep.
strings.dlg.dnd.s1_brawl.c2: [Rogue] Pick Steve's pocket during the fight. Then the other two. Then Baggy's.
strings.dlg.dnd.s1_brawl.c3: [Wizard] Cast Fireball. In the tavern. With everyone in it.
strings.dlg.dnd.s1_brawl.c4: [Paladin] Lecture the bandits on the moral consequences of banditry.
strings.dlg.dnd.s1_brawl_win:
The table hits Steve squarely. Steve hits the wall. The other two bandits look at Steve, look at you, and leave very quickly.

OAKHAVEN (GM): "Steve is unconscious. You may loot Steve."

ROLF: "Gerald would like to file Steve's tax return."
strings.dlg.dnd.s1_brawl_bard:
You sing. Your fictional voice soars. The bandits drop their weapons, put their arms round each other's shoulders and sway. One of them, Steve, sobs openly. They buy you a drink.

OAKHAVEN (GM): "Steve would like to join your party."

EVERYONE: "NO."
strings.dlg.dnd.s1_brawl_rogue:
In the confusion you lift three purses, a dagger, a love letter addressed to Steve, and Baggy's magnifying glass.

BAGGY: "My magnifying glass! There's a THIEF among us!"

YOU: "Shocking. We should investigate."

BAGGY: "YES. Partner!" You investigate together. You do not find the thief.
strings.dlg.dnd.s1_brawl_wizard:
OAKHAVEN (GM): "You cast Fireball in a small wooden tavern." He stares at you for a long time. "Roll damage. For everyone. Including yourself."

The fictional tavern burns down. The fictional bandits are very surprised. So is the fictional party. Marta's cleric heals everyone with bread, one slice at a time, muttering.

MARTA: "Every Thursday. EVERY Thursday somebody casts Fireball in the tavern."
strings.dlg.dnd.s1_brawl_paladin:
You deliver a stirring forty-minute lecture on the ethics of banditry, the social conditions that lead to it, and the importance of a good pension. The bandits, defeated, enrol in a correspondence course.

LORD ASHGRAVE (as Lord Definitely-Not-A-Vampire): "I too shall lecture."

OAKHAVEN (GM): "Please don't."
strings.dlg.dnd.s1_brawl_fail:
It goes badly. Very badly. In the end Hollis's character, Grizzlebeard, wins the fight by saying "Hmm" at the bandits until they leave.

OAKHAVEN (GM): "That... worked. I don't know why that worked."

HOLLIS: "Natural twenty."

OAKHAVEN (GM): "You didn't roll."
strings.dlg.dnd.s1_shop:
OAKHAVEN (GM): "Before you leave town, you may visit the general store."

Two hours later, the party is still in the general store.

Marta's cleric has bought fifty feet of rope, then another fifty feet "in case". Baggy has bought eleven magnifying glasses. Rolf has done a full audit of the shopkeeper's books and found a discrepancy. Ashgrave has bought a single black rose and refuses to explain why.

OAKHAVEN (GM, faintly): "And that's where we'll stop for tonight."

ROLF: "We haven't left the tavern."

OAKHAVEN (GM): "We never leave the tavern on the first session. It's tradition."
strings.dlg.dnd.s2_start:
OAKHAVEN (GM): "Session Two. The Dungeon of Mild Peril. You stand before a great stone door. Cold air breathes from the darkness beyond."

BAGGY: "I check for traps."

OAKHAVEN (GM): "On the door?"

BAGGY: "On everything. Every five feet. For the whole dungeon. I'm a very thorough Paladin."

OAKHAVEN (GM, sighing): "Fine. Everybody move very slowly. What's your plan?"
strings.dlg.dnd.s2_start.c0: [Classic] "I prod the floor ahead of us with a ten-foot pole."
strings.dlg.dnd.s2_start.c1: [Bold] "I walk confidently down the middle of the corridor."
strings.dlg.dnd.s2_trap:
The ten-foot pole taps a flagstone. CLICK. Forty arrows fly out of the walls and hit nothing but the pole.

OAKHAVEN (GM, through gritted teeth): "The pole. Is. Destroyed."

MARTA: "I've got another fifty feet of rope and a broom."

The party proceeds, poking everything with a broom.
strings.dlg.dnd.s2_trap_hit:
CLICK. Forty arrows fly out of the walls. You make a saving throw.

OAKHAVEN (GM): "You take... forty arrows."

Sister Crumb hands you a slice of bread. You are healed to one hit point, and very full.

BAGGY: "I did say I'd check for traps."
strings.dlg.dnd.s2_gerald:
ROLF (horrified, then resigned): "Gerald... goes first."

Gerald steps on a pressure plate. Gerald is fine; Gerald's armour is a cardigan, and the arrows pass harmlessly through the knitting.

OAKHAVEN (GM): "That is not how arrows work."

ROLF: "Gerald is very good at knitting."
strings.dlg.dnd.s2_room:
OAKHAVEN (GM): "You enter a chamber. In the centre stands a treasure chest. It is a very nice chest. It is, if anything, suspiciously nice."

LORD ASHGRAVE: "It's a mimic."

BAGGY: "It's DEFINITELY a mimic."

HOLLIS: "Mimic."

OAKHAVEN (GM, innocently): "It is a normal chest. What do you do?"
strings.dlg.dnd.s2_room.c0: [Rogue: Search it for traps] Use your thieves' tools on the 'lock'.
strings.dlg.dnd.s2_room.c1: [Search for treasure] Ignore the chest. Search the room for treasure.
strings.dlg.dnd.s2_room.c3: [Feed it] Give the chest a slice of Marta's bread and see what happens.
strings.dlg.dnd.s2_mimic_rogue:
Your lockpick goes into the keyhole. The keyhole licks it.

You withdraw the lockpick very slowly, pocket it, and back away, while the 'chest' grins at you with a mouth full of teeth.

OAKHAVEN (GM, disappointed): "...Fine. It's a mimic. Well spotted."
strings.dlg.dnd.s2_search:
You search the room for treasure.

OAKHAVEN (GM, leaning forward, in a deep and booming voice he has clearly been practising): "You find... NOTHING."

A beat.

"A WANDERING MONSTER APPEARS."

It is a very small goblin. It looks at the six of you, looks at the chest with teeth, and wanders off again.

OAKHAVEN (GM): "I'd been saving that for three years."
strings.dlg.dnd.s2_mimic:
You open the chest. The chest opens you.

OAKHAVEN (GM): "Roll a saving throw."

You roll. You survive, barely, smelling of chest. Rolf's accountant Gerald files an insurance claim on your behalf. It is denied.
strings.dlg.dnd.s2_mimic_bread:
You toss a slice of Marta's bread at the chest. The chest's lid snaps open, catches the bread out of the air, and closes again.

Then it makes a small happy noise, sidles over, and leans against your leg like a cat.

MARTA: "Aww."

OAKHAVEN (GM, defeated): "The mimic... is now your pet. It is called..."

BAGGY: "CHESTER."

OAKHAVEN (GM): "...It is called Chester."
strings.dlg.dnd.s2_puzzle:
OAKHAVEN (GM): "A great door bars your way. Carved into it is a riddle. 'I am tall when I am young, and short when I am old. What am I?' Answer correctly, and the door will open."

There is a long silence around the table. Rolf is counting on his fingers. Ashgrave whispers "Me?" Hollis says "Hmm" in a thoughtful sort of way.
strings.dlg.dnd.s2_riddle_win:
OAKHAVEN (GM): "...Correct." He looks genuinely surprised. "Nobody has ever got that."

YOU: "It's always a candle."

OAKHAVEN (GM, writing it down): "It's always a candle," he agrees softly. The door grinds open.
strings.dlg.dnd.s2_riddle_lose:
The door does not open. The riddle rearranges itself to say: 'NO.'

MARTA (gently): "It's a candle, dear."

OAKHAVEN (GM): "MARTA."

MARTA: "What? They looked so sad." The door opens anyway, out of pity.
strings.dlg.dnd.s2_riddle_door:
You hit the door. The door has an armour class of twenty-five. You hit it again. And again. Eventually Oakhaven, who has been watching the clock, says "The door gives up", and it does.

ROLF: "That was beautiful."
strings.dlg.dnd.s2_split:
OAKHAVEN (GM): "The corridor forks. Left: a faint smell of gold and brimstone. Right: a faint smell of... soup?"

Every player at the table turns to look at you.

BAGGY (whispering urgently): "Whatever you do, don't split the-"
strings.dlg.dnd.s2_split.c0: [Wisdom] "We stay together. Left, all of us."
strings.dlg.dnd.s2_split.c1: [Classic mistake] "Let's split up. We'll cover more ground."
strings.dlg.dnd.s2_split_bad:
The table goes silent. Hollis puts his head in his hands. Oakhaven's smile is slow, terrible, and completely professional.

Ten minutes later, three of you are hanging upside down in a net, Gerald is being audited by a goblin, and Lord Definitely-Not-A-Vampire has been accidentally exposed to sunlight via a conveniently placed skylight.

ASHGRAVE: "I SPARKLE."

OAKHAVEN (GM): "You take no damage, but your dignity takes four."

You regroup, eventually, at the dragon's door.
strings.dlg.dnd.s2_end:
OAKHAVEN (GM): "You stand at the threshold of a vast cavern. Gold, everywhere. Mountains of it. And on the largest mountain, asleep, curled around a single glittering amulet..."

He reaches behind the screen and produces the dragon: a red-painted salt shaker with paper wings.

"...DEBTRAX THE INSOLVENT. One eye opens." He puts the salt shaker down with a heavy click. "And that's where we'll stop for tonight."

The whole table screams.
strings.dlg.dnd.s3_start:
The back table is packed. Word has got around. Fenwick is watching from behind a bookshelf he has brought for the purpose. Kaelen is taking notes. Sabrino has provided snacks shaped like dice.

OAKHAVEN (GM): "Session Three. The salt shaker... I mean, DEBTRAX THE INSOLVENT rises from his hoard. His voice is like a landslide in a counting-house."

He does the voice. It is unexpectedly terrifying.

OAKHAVEN (as DEBTRAX): "WHO DARES DISTURB MY ACCOUNTS?"
strings.dlg.dnd.s3_start.c1: [Talk] "We come in peace. Mostly. About the amulet..."
strings.dlg.dnd.s3_fight:
OAKHAVEN (GM): "Debtrax breathes fire. Everyone make a saving throw."

HOLLIS (instantly): "Twenty."

OAKHAVEN (GM): "Hollis. That's a six-sided die."

HOLLIS: "It's a big six."

The fire washes over the party. It's your turn.
strings.dlg.dnd.s3_fight.c0: [Roll: Athletics] Charge the dragon with everything you have.
strings.dlg.dnd.s3_fight_win:
Your dice hit the table and come up a nineteen. The whole back table of the Lantern Inn erupts. Rolf knocks over the tea. Baggy stands on a chair. Marta screams "GET HIM!" in a voice that has stopped tavern brawls for seventeen years.

OAKHAVEN (GM, slowly, with deep respect): "Debtrax the Insolvent... is defeated."
strings.dlg.dnd.s3_fight_team:
Everyone at the table rolls at once. Six dice clatter across the wood, and every single one comes up high, even Hollis's, which for once is clearly an honest twenty-sided die.

HOLLIS (quietly): "...Huh. Didn't need to cheat."

OAKHAVEN (GM): "Debtrax the Insolvent falls. Together."
strings.dlg.dnd.s3_tpk:
Your dice skitter off the table, bounce off the teapot, and land on a one.

OAKHAVEN (GM, very gently): "Debtrax breathes fire again. That's... a total party kill."

A terrible silence falls over the table. Rolf's eyes fill with tears. Gerald. Poor Gerald.

Then Oakhaven looks round at all of them, sighs, and turns over a card from behind his screen.

OAKHAVEN (GM): "...But a passing cleric of the Last Dawn happens to be walking past the dungeon, entirely by coincidence, with a big bag of resurrection bread."

MARTA: "That's me! That's Sister Crumb!"

OAKHAVEN (GM): "Yes. It is. Somehow. Roll again."
strings.dlg.dnd.s3_tpk.c0: [Second chance] Roll again. Together, this time.
strings.dlg.dnd.s3_talk: OAKHAVEN (as DEBTRAX): "TALK? No adventurer has ever tried to TALK to me. They usually just stab." The salt shaker leans in. "Very well. Speak."
strings.dlg.dnd.s3_talk.c0: [Roll: Persuasion] "You stole the Amulet of Unpaid Taxes. We'd like to settle the account. Fairly."
strings.dlg.dnd.s3_talk.c1: [Gerald] Let Rolf's accountant do the talking.
strings.dlg.dnd.s3_talk_win:
OAKHAVEN (as DEBTRAX): "Fairly? FAIRLY?" A long pause. "In four hundred years, nobody has ever offered to settle anything fairly."

The salt shaker settles back onto its hoard. "Take the amulet. And tell the Treasury... tell them I was always going to give it back. I was just waiting for someone to ask nicely."

Around the table there is a stunned silence. Then Baggy starts clapping. Then everyone is clapping.
strings.dlg.dnd.s3_talk_audit:
ROLF (as Gerald, adjusting imaginary spectacles): "Mr. Insolvent. I've reviewed your hoard. Four hundred years of undeclared income. No receipts. No depreciation schedule."

OAKHAVEN (as DEBTRAX, nervously): "I'm a DRAGON."

ROLF: "The law doesn't care, sir."

Twenty minutes later the dragon has agreed to a payment plan, handed over the amulet as collateral, and is weeping quietly into its gold.

ROLF (out of character, glowing): "I have never been so powerful."
strings.dlg.dnd.s3_bard:
You stand up from the table. In character. You clear your throat. You begin to sing.

OAKHAVEN (GM): "You're seducing the dragon."

YOU: "I'm seducing the dragon."

OAKHAVEN (GM, closing his eyes): "There is a gravestone at Hollowmere about this exact thing."

YOU (still singing): "I know."
strings.dlg.dnd.s3_bard_win:
The high note rings out across the Lantern Inn. Marta drops a plate. Fenwick, behind his bookshelf, forgets to shush anybody.

OAKHAVEN (as DEBTRAX, slowly): "...I am going to write you letters. So many letters."

The dragon gives you the amulet, a lock of its, um, dragon hair, and a poem. The poem is very bad. You keep it anyway.
strings.dlg.dnd.s3_bard_lose:
The high note cracks. The dragon winces. Then, to everyone's surprise, laughs: a huge, rumbling, salt-shaker laugh.

OAKHAVEN (as DEBTRAX): "Nobody has made me laugh in four hundred years. Take the amulet. Take it! Just never sing again."
strings.dlg.dnd.s3_end:
OAKHAVEN (GM): "And so the heroes returned the Amulet of Unpaid Taxes to the Royal Treasury, where it was promptly filed, stamped, and lost again."

He lowers the dragon screen. Behind it, it turns out, is a whole little world: hand-drawn maps, a painted salt-shaker dragon, notes in neat Bureau handwriting going back years. Years of Thursdays.

"That's the end of the campaign," he says, and for once his voice isn't quite steady. "Thank you. All of you. I've been writing this for nine years. You're the first group that ever finished it."
strings.dlg.dnd.s3_end.c0: End of campaign. Take a bow.
strings.dlg.dnd.s3_end.c1: End of campaign. Take a bow.
strings.dlg.dnd.s3_bow_great:
The whole back table stands up and gives the Game Master a round of applause. Oakhaven takes off his spectacles, cleans them for much longer than spectacles need, and puts them back on.

Then he hands you a single twenty-sided die, worn smooth, the numbers nearly rubbed away.

"My first die," he says. "It always rolled well for people who deserved it. And the screen, too. I'll make a new one. I'm starting a new campaign."
strings.dlg.dnd.s3_bow:
Everybody applauds. Hollis applauds loudest, which surprises everyone, including Hollis.

Oakhaven hands you his first die, worn smooth with years of Thursdays, and his old dragon screen.

"Keep them," he says. "I'm starting a new campaign. Same time next week?"
strings.dlg.dnd.after:
Oakhaven straightens a stack of papers that is already straight.

"The next campaign is called 'The Lich Who Forgot to File'. It is set in the Underdark. There is a riddle. It is a candle." A very small smile. "Every Thursday, after the office closes. Bring dice. Bring snacks."

"And bring Hollis honest dice. I've given up asking him."

strings.item.lucky_d20.description: A twenty-sided die worn smooth by years of Thursdays. It always rolled well for people who deserved it. +2 to every dice roll in conversation, +2% critical chance.
strings.item.gm_screen.name: The Game Master's Screen
strings.item.gm_screen.description: A folding screen painted with dragons and tax tables. Surprisingly good at stopping arrows. Held up, it makes you feel like you know something everyone else doesn't.
